summary:
Roraima stands under Brazil's national framework, which the parent record carries in full. Two instruments specific to this state appear in the sources. State Ordinance No. 1,797/2023 addresses homophobia. On 9 August 2023 a law published in the Official Gazette of Boa Vista, approved by Mayor Genilson Costa of the Solidarity party, prohibited transgender athletes from competing in sports according to their gender identity.

No further region-specific signal on policing, custody placement, health-care access or violence against trans people was identified. On those questions the national assessment applies unchanged.
tangentialFactors: The Boa Vista measure is municipal, so it governs within the capital's jurisdiction rather than across Roraima. The state-level instrument, Ordinance No. 1,797/2023, is framed around homophobia rather than gender identity, and the sources do not state whether it names trans residents expressly or what it provides beyond its stated purpose.
localsOnly: The Boa Vista measure of 9 August 2023 falls on trans residents competing in local sport in the capital rather than on visitors passing through. State Ordinance No. 1,797/2023 is the state-level instrument residents can cite against homophobia; the sources do not record which state body receives complaints under it, what penalty it carries, or any case in which it has been applied.
outOfScopeNotes: No record of enforcement, court challenge or repeal of the Boa Vista measure was identified, and whether it remains in force is unresolved. The sources contain no Roraima-specific data on custody placement, health-care access, hate-crime enforcement or violence against trans people. The only geographic differentiation they offer is a national-level contrast between major cities and smaller or rural areas, which does not name this state.
